pharm: The more potent enantiomer of milnacipran; a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor with relatively greater potency for norepinephrine than serotonin reuptake inhibition, formulated as an extended-release capsule for once-daily treatment of major depressive disorder.
quick: Start 20 mg once daily x2 days, then 40 mg once daily; range 40-120 mg/day
May be taken with or without food; swallow whole, do not open/crush/chew
Limited data; neonatal adaptation/poor neonatal effects with 3rd-trimester use
Milnacipran detected in human milk; monitor infant for irritability/poor feeding
Moderate (CrCl 30-59) max 80 mg/day; severe (CrCl 15-29) max 40 mg/day; ESRD not recommended
No dose adjustment for mild, moderate, or severe impairment
Avoid; alcohol may cause rapid release (dose dumping) of the extended-release capsule
Suicidality/mood, blood pressure, heart rate, serotonin syndrome, bleeding
summary: Levomilnacipran (Fetzima) is an extended-release SNRI approved for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults. It carries a boxed warning for increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults. Dosing starts at 20 mg once daily for 2 days, increases to 40 mg once daily, and may be titrated in 40 mg increments to a maximum of 120 mg/day. It raises blood pressure and heart rate, so cardiovascular parameters must be monitored. It is contraindicated with MAOIs (serotonin syndrome risk) and the dose is capped in moderate-to-severe renal impairment. Discontinue gradually to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
indications: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults

dosage.n: Then increase to 40 mg once daily
Increase in 40 mg increments at intervals of >=2 days based on response/tolerability; max 120 mg/day

admin: Take once daily at approximately the same time each day, with or without food
Swallow capsules whole - do not open, chew, or crush
Titrate slowly per the recommended schedule based on response and tolerability
Do not stop abruptly - taper gradually to reduce discontinuation symptoms
Allow a 14-day washout after stopping an MAOI before starting, and 7 days after stopping levomilnacipran before starting an MAOI
moa: Levomilnacipran is the more active enantiomer of milnacipran and is a potent and selective inhibitor of serotonin (5-HT) and norepinephrine (NE) reuptake transporters in the central nervous system, with relatively greater potency for norepinephrine reuptake inhibition than serotonin reuptake inhibition. By blocking presynaptic reuptake it increases synaptic concentrations of both monoamines, which is believed to underlie its antidepressant effect. It has no significant affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic, or adrenergic receptors. The precise mechanism of its antidepressant action is not fully understood.

absolute: Concomitant use of monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or use within 14 days of stopping an MAOI, due to serotonin syndrome risk
Initiation in patients being treated with linezolid or intravenous methylene blue
Known hypersensitivity to levomilnacipran, milnacipran, or any component
relative: Pre-existing hypertension or cardiac disease (raises BP and heart rate)
History of seizures, mania/bipolar disorder, or increased bleeding risk
Volume depletion or concomitant diuretics (hyponatremia/SIADH risk)
monitor: Suicidal ideation/behavior, especially early in therapy and after dose changes
Blood pressure and heart rate before and during treatment
Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs
Serum sodium in at-risk patients; signs of abnormal bleeding

preg: There are insufficient human data to inform risk; animal studies showed increased neonatal pup mortality at exposures about 5 times the maximum recommended human dose. Neonates exposed to SNRIs/SSRIs late in the third trimester have developed complications requiring prolonged hospitalization, respiratory support, and tube feeding (poor neonatal adaptation). Use late in pregnancy may increase the risk of postpartum hemorrhage. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. A pregnancy registry exists.
lact: Milnacipran (the racemic parent) is present in human milk; data on levomilnacipran are limited. Breastfed infants should be monitored for agitation, irritability, poor feeding, and poor weight gain. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Dosing must be capped in renal impairment: no adjustment for mild impairment (CrCl 60-89 mL/min); maximum 80 mg once daily for moderate impairment (CrCl 30-59); maximum 40 mg once daily for severe impairment (CrCl 15-29). Use is not recommended in end-stage renal disease (CrCl <15 mL/min).
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for patients with mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment.

major: MAOIs / linezolid / IV methylene blue - serotonin syndrome (contraindicated)
Other serotonergic drugs (triptans, SSRIs/SNRIs, TCAs, tramadol, fentanyl, lithium, buspirone, St. John's Wort) - serotonin syndrome
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - increase exposure; cap dose at 80 mg/day
moderate: Anticoagulants/antiplatelets (warfarin, aspirin, NSAIDs) - increased bleeding risk
Diuretics/other drugs causing hyponatremia - additive SIADH/hyponatremia risk
minor: No clinically important effect on most CYP-metabolized substrates at usual doses
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not require dose change.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it may cause rapid (dose-dumping) release of the extended-release formulation and worsen CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase blood pressure and heart rate readings; no characteristic assay interference.

emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Suicidal ideation/behavior and clinical worsening, especially in the first weeks and after dose changes
Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline and periodically
Serum sodium in older or volume-depleted patients
Signs of bleeding when used with anticoagulants/antiplatelets
counsel: Take once a day at the same time; swallow the capsule whole - do not open or crush it
It may take several weeks to feel the full benefit; keep taking it as prescribed
Watch for worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm, especially when starting or changing dose, and seek help immediately
Do not stop suddenly - your doctor will lower the dose gradually to avoid withdrawal effects
Avoid alcohol, which can cause the medicine to release too quickly
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially other antidepressants, triptans, tramadol, or MAOIs, and report agitation, fever, or muscle stiffness right away
pearls: BOXED WARNING: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults - monitor closely early in therapy
More noradrenergic than most SNRIs - watch blood pressure and heart rate
Renal dosing caps: 80 mg/day if CrCl 30-59, 40 mg/day if CrCl 15-29; no hepatic adjustment
Cap at 80 mg/day with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
Approved only for MDD (unlike milnacipran, which is approved for fibromyalgia)
Taper to discontinue; abrupt stop causes dizziness, nausea, irritability, paresthesia
missed: If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Experience is limited. Overdose with SNRIs may cause serotonin syndrome, seizures, changes in consciousness, tachycardia, hypertension or hypotension, and ECG changes. There is no specific antidote. Manage with airway, breathing, and circulation support; cardiac and vital-sign monitoring; activated charcoal if appropriate; and supportive/symptomatic care. Due to the large volume of distribution, dialysis is unlikely to be beneficial. Contact a poison control center.
